author: Raymond Baccari
title: Business owner Gregory Stevens announces 2026 run for governor - NewsBreak
text:
By Raymond Baccari No media credit provided. ,
35 minutes ago
EAST PROVIDENCE, R.I. (WPRI) — Local restaurant owner Gregory Stevens has entered Rhode Island’s 2026 race for governor, joining what is now a multi-candidate Democratic primary.
Stevens, who owns Pat’s Italian Restaurants, filed paperwork with the R.I. Board of Elections Wednesday morning. He is the third Democrat to throw a hat into the ring, along with incumbent Gov. Dan McKee and former CVS executive Helena Foulkes.
Stevens told 12 News Wednesday that he’s running because he thinks people’s “needs aren’t being met.”
The 66-year-old business owner said his policy goals include helping seniors, diversity and inclusion, and bringing in more tourism money to the state. (His website also lists out his stances on other issues such as the 2nd Amendment and immigration.)
“I’m a big proponent of tourism and taking in as many dollars as we can,” Stevens explained, arguing the state leaves “a lot of sales and use dollars” on the table.
Stevens registered to vote in Rhode Island earlier this month, according to the secretary of state’s office. He said that he moved to Wakefield four years ago and before that lived in Attleboro.
Stevens didn’t have much to say about McKee and Foulkes. When asked his thoughts on McKee’s tenure as governor, Stevens said he hasn’t seen much change happen, and he said he didn’t know much about the former CVS executive.
On the failed westbound Washington Bridge, Stevens said that “someone needs to be held accountable,” and that it “starts at the top.” He said he would also remove R.I. Department of Transportation Director Peter Alviti from his position.
The most recent public poll for the brewing Democratic primary was an “Ocean State Poll” released by the University of New Hampshire Survey Center last month, which showed McKee trailing Foulkes in a head-to-head matchup. McKee got support from 19% of respondents in that poll, while Foulkes had 35%, with 40% of those polled undecided.
Both Foulkes and McKee currently hold financial advantages over Stevens. As of Sept. 30, Foulkes has $2.4 million in her campaign account, while McKee has $1 million. (Another potential candidate, House Speaker Joe Shekarchi, has $4.1 million on hand.)
“Those figures don’t scare me,” Stevens said.
On the Republican side, Smithfield resident Elaine Pelino has announced her candidacy. Other potential GOP candidates include Ashley Kalus, the party’s 2022 nominee, as well as 2022 GOP nominee for lieutenant governor Aaron Guckian and Senate Minority Leader Jessica de la Cruz.
The primary is Sept. 8, 2026.
